editorial.headline: A Nationally Open Agency Activity, Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Guarantee-marketing agents can operate across every listed scale nationally, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium closes this activity to a Bali address.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the marketing of guarantee-business activities for and on behalf of a guarantee company or an Islamic guarantee company. Its centre of gravity is agency: the registered business promotes the guarantee company’s activity under that company’s name, rather than presenting an undefined commercial role. The scope is therefore precise about both the work—marketing—and the relationship within which it is done.

Nationally, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. It is also open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That combination gives the code a broad national frame: it recognises an agency function that may be registered from the smallest listed scale through to the largest, while retaining the same defined role of marketing for a guarantee company or Islamic guarantee company.

Bali is the decisive exception. A foreign investor cannot register this activity at a Bali address today. Although the national status is open, the Besar scale is classified as Medium-Low risk, and Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration. The restriction is island-wide and permanent under the Bali PMA moratorium, reflected in the activity’s Bali status as closed because of that moratorium. National openness is real, but it does not overcome Bali’s island-wide PMA moratorium.

For founders, the distinction is not cosmetic. The national setting permits up to full foreign ownership and lists every business scale as open; the Bali setting prevents PMA registration for this activity altogether. The relevant question is therefore not whether the activity is nationally open in principle, but whether the proposed business address is in Bali. For a Bali address, the record’s answer is unambiguous: the PMA route is blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is real, but it does not overcome Bali’s island-wide PMA moratorium.
